oneLiner: The clear No. 2 custom AI silicon and optical interconnect franchise, now guiding to ~$18B FY28 with a signed, expanded Google agreement - and a stock that fell 8-10% on the beat anyway because expectations had run further still.
thesis: AI demand keeps accelerating. Q2 FY27 revenue was a record $2.739B (+37% YoY, +13% QoQ), Q3 is guided to $3.15B (+50%+ YoY), and FY27 was raised to ~$12B (+~45%) with FY28 set at ~$18B (+~50%).
Custom XPU pipeline is converting. Custom silicon is expected to ramp significantly in H2 FY27 on the tier-1 XPU program plus 10+ XPU-attach programs, on top of AWS Trainium and Microsoft Maia work.

Electro-optics is a second growth engine. Marvell disclosed $1B of supply-capacity prepayments to secure 1.6T optical DSP and 51.2T switch supply - management is betting real balance sheet on the demand.
Celestial AI adds a scale-up optics option. The $3.25B Photonic Fabric acquisition (closed Feb 2, 2026) targets a ~$500M annual run-rate exiting FY28, ~$1B exiting FY29.

Google has converted from rumor to contract. On the Aug 27 call Marvell announced an expanded commercial agreement with a key hyperscaler (widely reported as Google) covering custom programs including XPU-attach, with significant revenue potential in FY2029 and beyond.

latestProse: Q2 FY27 revenue was a record $2.739B, +37% YoY and +13% QoQ, $39M above the guide midpoint, with data center at $2.172B (+46% YoY, 79% of revenue) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.94 on $865.9M of non-GAAP net income (+40% YoY). Management raised FY27 revenue to ~$12B and set FY28 at ~$18B, and disclosed $1B of prepayments to lock down 1.6T optics and 51.2T switch supply. The stock still dropped 8-10% the next day - a beat-and-raise was not enough for where the shares had run. The disclosure that matters most: the expanded commercial agreement with a key hyperscaler (reported to be Google) covering custom programs including XPU-attach - the Google option is now a signed agreement, but its 'significant revenue in FY2029 and beyond' framing is exactly the payoff timeline the market balked at.
guidanceProse: Q3 FY27 guide: revenue $3.15B plus or minus 5% (midpoint +15% QoQ, +50%+ YoY), non-GAAP gross margin 57.5-58.5% (GAAP 52.9-53.9%), non-GAAP EPS $1.10 plus or minus $0.05. FY27 revenue outlook raised to ~$12B (~45% growth) and FY28 to ~$18B (~50% growth). Management guided gross margin to stay in the 57.5-58.5% range through FY28 as the high-volume custom ramp creates a structural mix headwind - the growth is real but it arrives at below-corporate margins. The debate: whether the Aug 28 selloff on a clean beat-and-raise is healthy digestion after a huge run, or the start of multiple compression for the whole custom-silicon trade as payoffs (Google in FY29) stretch out.

guide.label: Q3 FY27 revenue guide
guide.sub: Midpoint +50%+ YoY; non-GAAP EPS $1.10; FY27 ~$12B, FY28 ~$18B

segments: Data center: $2.172B, 79% of Q2 FY27 revenue, +46% YoY (custom compute, electro-optics, switching, storage)
Communications and other: ~$567M, ~21% of revenue (derived from total minus data center)
Within data center, custom silicon ramps significantly in H2 FY27; interconnect rides the 800G-to-1.6T optics transition
competitive: Broadcom: dominant custom-ASIC rival (Google TPU deal through 2031); Marvell holds ~20-25% of custom ASIC design share
Alchip/MediaTek: lower-cost back-end design challengers; alleged Trainium 3/4 back-end losses remain the key bear claim
Nvidia: merchant-silicon gravity plus NVLink Fusion ecosystem shapes hyperscaler make-vs-buy
Astera Labs/Credo: niche connectivity competitors; Marvell leads PAM4 optical DSPs
Customer set: AWS (Trainium), Microsoft (Maia), Meta, and now an expanded Google custom agreement across 18+ reported design wins
moat: Deep multi-generation co-design relationships with hyperscalers, leading PAM4 optical DSP and 224G SerDes IP, and Celestial's Photonic Fabric plus XConn CXL switching give Marvell a full electrical-plus-optical interconnect stack few can match. The $1B in supply prepayments adds a capacity moat competitors must now match. Switching costs on in-flight XPU programs are high, though the alleged Trainium loss shows the moat is per-socket, not permanent.
risks: Socket churn. Reported (unconfirmed) loss of AWS Trainium 3/4 back-end work to Alchip; custom ASIC wins are contestable every generation.
Extreme concentration. Data center is 79% of revenue, dominated by a handful of hyperscalers; one program cancellation moves the model.
Google payoff is back-loaded. The expanded agreement points to significant revenue in FY2029 and beyond - two-plus years of execution risk before it shows up in the P&L.
Structural margin mix. Gross margin guided to 57.5-58.5% through FY28 as custom scales; the growth dilutes the margin profile.
Thin GAAP economics. Heavy SBC, amortization, and acquisition costs; Celestial adds ~27M shares plus up to $2.25B earnouts.
High-beta AI trade. An 8-10% one-day drop on a beat-and-raise shows how little cushion the multiple leaves.
catalysts: Oct 6, 2026: Investor Day - custom pipeline, Google agreement detail, and Celestial roadmap expected
Late Nov/early Dec 2026: Q3 FY27 results ($3.15B guide) - first proof of the H2 custom ramp
Through FY27: 1.6T optical DSP and 51.2T switch ramp against the $1B prepaid capacity
FY28: delivery against the ~$18B revenue target; Google custom program milestones toward FY29 revenue
pricedIn: MRVL closed around $241 on Aug 28 after the 8-10% post-earnings drop (some sources report $217; exact close unverified - sources conflict). At roughly $210B market cap the stock pays up front for the raised ~$12B FY27 outlook and much of the ~$18B FY28 target; consensus stayed bullish post-print (Barclays, UBS, Wells Fargo, Citi all reiterated). The debate is no longer whether Google converts - it did - but whether an FY29-and-beyond payoff justifies today's multiple, and whether 57.5-58.5% structural gross margins deserve Broadcom-style valuation treatment.

scenarios.bear: AI capex digests in 2027, the H2 custom ramp underwhelms, and contested sockets (Trainium back-end) resurface; FY28 lands nearer $14-15B than $18B. The multiple compresses toward 30x on cut estimates; stock revisits the $150-170 area.
scenarios.base: FY27 delivers ~$12B with the Q3 $3.15B step-up on schedule; the custom ramp and 1.6T optics cycle track toward ~$18B FY28. The stock chops through digestion and grinds to new highs as the Oct 6 Investor Day and Q3 print de-risk the roadmap.
scenarios.bull: The Google agreement scales into confirmed FY29 programs alongside retained AWS/Microsoft sockets, validating a $10B+ custom business; Celestial wins scale-up optical sockets. Estimates move materially higher and the stock clears $330 decisively.

valPresets.note: FCF basis works here (strong operating cash flow), but the $1B supply prepayments and Celestial earnouts are real cash claims, and GAAP earnings remain a fraction of non-GAAP - SBC is a cost the DCF ignores.
